scope: Proposition F.2 (Canonical forms under degeneration) of the manuscript “Uniform Cartier sections for Fano type contractions” (preprints/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 066 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d97ba60373419ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 74. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses preceding Lemma F.1, S0 has a divisor-free reflexive canonical generator ω0. It has the G-character of ω. It is homogeneous for Tw, and its weight κ satisfies ⟨w, κ⟩ = AS(w). (F.3) If an additional torus acts on the original germ, preserves w, and makes ω homogeneous, its character is preserved separately. None of these assertions assumes AS(w) = w(h). Moreover the action of G on S0 is quasi-étale.
